paragraphs: Friend, here's what this psalm teaches me: the waiting is not wasted. David waited, and the LORD inclined to him and heard his cry (Psalm 40:1). Then the LORD lifted him out of the pit and set his feet upon a rock (Psalm 40:2). The waiting felt long, but God was never far from it.

But look at the second half, because it's honest. The man who just sang a new song says evils without number surround him, and then he asks, "O LORD, do not withhold Your mercy from me" (Psalm 40:11-12). Praise and neediness live in the same song, friend. You don't have to finish being rescued before you start singing, and you don't have to hide your need to prove your faith. David even says, "But I am poor and needy; may the Lord think of me" (Psalm 40:17).

So what does David lean on? Not his offerings, but a heart that delights to do God's will (Psalm 40:6-8). Not his own strength, but the One he calls "my helper and deliverer" (Psalm 40:17). Hebrews says Christ spoke the words of verses 6 to 8 (Hebrews 10:5-7), which tells me this song points to Jesus. So when you're stuck in your own pit, baker, keep waiting, keep singing and keep asking, because the One who hears has already come.
